paper_metadata.title: Genetically Engineered Quantum Circuits for Financial Market Indicators

summary: The paper studies GASP-based approximate state preparation for a 4-qubit encoding of stock-return data from four stocks (XOM, WMT, PG, MSFT) over rolling 4-month windows, then applies VQSVD with one-layer Rz/Ry + CNOT circuits to estimate SVD entropy. It reports target fidelities of 70% to 99% and finds diminishing returns above about 90% fidelity, with no formal quantum speedup or practical advantage demonstrated.

experiments.description: Approximate state preparation of stock-price return data using GASP, followed by VQSVD to compute SVD entropy for four real stocks over rolling 4x4 monthly windows; compared against qGAN and AAE baselines, with results reported for multiple target fidelities and on simulated and real quantum hardware.

algorithm.variant: GASP-generated approximate state preparation combined with VQSVD
algorithm.ansatz: Parameterized single-qubit Rz/Ry layers with linear CNOT entanglement for the QSVD unitaries U(θ) and V(θ′); GASP-generated state-preparation circuit before QSVD
algorithm.convergence_criteria: not specified; optimization performed for each target fidelity until circuit generation/parameter optimization completed
algorithm.parameter_initialization: GASP target circuit initialized from genetic search; QSVD parameters initialized as random values

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Stock return matrix a_nt loaded into a 4-qubit state |data> = sum_{n=1}^4 sum_{t=1}^4 a_nt |n> |t>, with 2 qubits for stock index and 2 qubits for time index
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize LSVD(θ,θ′) = sum_{q=1}^{ns} (1 - <σ_z^q σ_z^{q+ns}> / 2) to transform the Schmidt basis to the computational basis and recover singular values for SVD entropy

problem_instance.description: Rolling-window SVD entropy estimation from monthly stock opening prices and log returns

dataset_specification.preprocessing: monthly opening prices converted to logarithmic returns; correlation matrices formed from normalized returns; 4-stock by 4-time-step windows used for state preparation

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute log returns r_nt = ln(s_nt) - ln(s_n,t-1); normalize to a_nt; form correlation matrix C_nm = sum_t a_nt a_mt; use 4-month rolling windows (Apr-Aug, May-Sep, Jun-Oct, Jul-Nov, etc.)
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare ideal SVD entropy (from diagonalized correlation matrix) against qGAN, AAE, and GASP across target fidelities; report statevector fidelity, loss curves, Frobenius-norm reconstruction error, and mean squared error of entropy

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical computation of log returns, correlation matrices, and target statevectors; GASP used to generate approximate state-preparation circuits
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Diagonalization of reconstructed correlation matrix; computation of SVD entropy and mean squared error versus ideal entropy

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: loss curves shown for QSVD optimization; exact numeric final loss not reported

speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic or empirical speedup is quantified. The paper claims improved fidelity and lower depth/resource usage, but does not provide a formal speedup factor.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 4 qubits for the stock/time encoding; one-layer QSVD circuits; GASP target fidelities 70%, 75%, 80%, 85%, 90%, 95%, 99%
limiting_factors: No asymptotic or empirical speedup factor is reported
Problem size is tiny: 4 stocks x 4 time steps on 4 qubits
Classical preprocessing and optimization dominate much of the workflow
The paper emphasizes fidelity/resource tradeoffs rather than advantage over classical methods
Comparison baselines are qGAN and AAE, not a strong classical finance solver

notes: Hardware type inferred as simulator_statevector for the 'simulated and real quantum computer' experiments because the paper explicitly mentions both but does not name the simulator/QPU in the provided text; the experiment description aggregates the reported simulated and real-hardware runs as one study.
num_qubits reported from the 4-stock/4-time-step encoding into a 4-qubit state vector (2 qubits stock + 2 qubits time).
Circuit depth not numerically reported; only that GASP circuits have low depth and QSVD unitaries use one layer.
No asymptotic speedup analysis is provided; the paper is an application/feasibility study.
The paper reports improved fidelity and lower depth for GASP-generated state preparation, but does not demonstrate quantum advantage over classical finance methods.
The experiment is a small-scale feasibility study on 4 qubits, so it falls in the small QPU/NISQ category.
